doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Copying scores for the black English composer Reginald Forsythe
summary: As a teenager Hinton copied Deep Forest and other scores for Forsythe at the Ritz Hotel, who was writing for Paul Whiteman.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. It was an old theatre, it was the Peerless Theatre, that was the name of it. And I would go by the rehearsals. One of the things that I am very proud of, remember the name Reginald Forthsyte?
Right. He wrote a theme song called Deep Forest.

He wrote that. This is the era that I am talking about. When I was a kid I wanted to be around everybody that was musical and the place was the Ritz Hotel. He stayed in the Ritz Hotel and he needed somebody… he was writing this theme song and some things for Paul Whiteman. He asked me, “Can you copy?” And I said, “Yes sir.” And so I copied some of the scores for him. And it was amazing to me because here was guy, he was a Black Englishman with a handkerchief in his sleeve. That‟s how I got to know Reginald Forthsyte. But to get back to Louis Armstrong…
Before you get to Louie, Reginald Forthsyte, you said he was Black?
Yeah he was Black. He was a Black Englishman.
He studied under [unintelligible] and under [unintelligible] too.
Oh boy that‟s wonderful. Because he is a wonderful musician, very respectful here as well as over there.

Yes he was. He wrote Serenade for Paul Whiteman‟s band. I had the pleasure in my youth…and it was through these rehearsals that I got a chance to sit there and be delighted to make the…copy the score for Deep Forest.
